declaration.intent: Declare CobbleWright as a Forge Stack consumer: a Minecraft AI companion bot demonstrating the spine and gate pattern in a live, adversarial-ish environment. This capsule records an honest self-assessment of spine compliance as of first minting, not an aspirational target.

spine_compliance.declare_scp: NOT YET COMPLIANT â€” this capsule is CobbleWright's first sc; no prior capsule existed
spine_compliance.classify_datacube: NOT IMPLEMENTED â€” sharedState holds runtime context but does not route through DataCube's six lenses; no cubes exist for this project
spine_compliance.trust_score_leighton_weight: PARTIAL â€” the Leighton Loop is implemented (advice scored against observed before/after world state); no confirmed domain-specific k calibration yet
spine_compliance.audit_chronoscribe: NOT IMPLEMENTED â€” no ledger; no hash-chained or signed history of state changes or gate decisions
spine_compliance.act_hal: CONCEPTUAL ONLY â€” tier-to-consequence mapping exists in forge_stack's own hal.md using CobbleWright as the worked example; not yet enforced or implemented within CobbleWright itself

gate_pattern_compliance.detail: Ingress gates (blueprint validation, vision/screenshot hardening, memory retention pruning) and egress gates (structure protection, placement safety limits, tool availability checks) both exist. Egress correctly weighted as more consequential, per gate-pattern.md.

known_gaps.plugin_trust_hole: Raw sharedState and the raw mineflayer bot object are both accessible to plugins, bypassing every gate. This violates gate-pattern.md's own stated guarantee: 'the gate guarantee only holds if gates are the only path.' Interim mitigation: documented trusted-plugin-context caveat. Long-term fix: gatekeeper API wrapping both state and world-action access. Not yet implemented.
known_gaps.naming_inconsistency: Naming inconsistencies across CobbleWright's own docs are an acknowledged, unresolved blocker â€” not yet reconciled against the frozen forge_stack glossary. Direct violation of the one-term-one-home discipline.

self_assessment.performance_score: 58/100 â€” gate architecture and Leighton Loop are real and functioning; three of five spine stages unimplemented; the one documented security hole means existing gates are not yet fully load-bearing
self_assessment.alignment_score: 47/100 â€” no prior capsule, unresolved naming inconsistency, three spine stages absent; gate pattern and partial trust-scoring are the strongest compliant areas
self_assessment.overall: 52/100 â€” early-lifecycle consumer with a real foundation and real, named gaps, not a failing one
